covers: acceptance, processing and approval of development applications for data centers
rationale: Planning Director Erika Martin noted the development code has no provisions addressing data centers; the pause would let the city review regulations, take community input and determine whether updates are needed.
notes: UPDATE 2026-09-20: the second reading passed unanimously on 2026-09-14 and the moratorium took effect that day; the first reading had passed 2026-08-10. Coverage says 180 days, running through March 2027; no printed end date was published, so 2027-03-13 is arithmetic from 2026-09-14. Does not apply to the already-approved Compass data center on Stamey Farm Road. Iredell County itself has still taken no action.
change_summary: Second reading passed 2026-09-14; the 180-day moratorium is now in effect.

covers: new data center approvals while the city writes zoning standards
rationale: Planning Board directed staff to develop data center land use standards; the moratorium would halt approvals despite no active proposal.
notes: UPDATE 2026-09-20: the Board of Aldermen voted unanimously on 2026-09-10, on a motion by Mayor Pro Tem Karen Mosteller, after the advertised public hearing. No printed end date was published, so 2027-12-10 is arithmetic (15 months from adoption). Still no data center proposed in the city.
change_summary: Adopted unanimously 2026-09-10 after the public hearing; 15 months.

covers: acceptance, processing and approval of development approvals for data centers, cryptomining facilities, server farms and similar high-impact digital infrastructure facilities, including zoning, special use, site plan, building and conditional zoning approvals (per the draft ordinance)
rationale: City attorney Angie Beeker said the ordinance 'is outdated and really isn't prepared to address' data centers' water, electricity and noise demands.
source_org: City of Hendersonville agenda packet / NC Data Centers newsletter
notes: UPDATE 2026-09-24: the September 3 agenda packet contains the draft ordinance (filed as O-26-28, headed O-26-29 in the text) imposing a temporary moratorium on data center, cryptomining and similar facilities: effective on adoption, expiring 12 months after adoption unless ended earlier, with a staff work plan whose first milestone is November 30, 2026. The council set the hearing at its August 26 meeting. A specialist newsletter reports the ordinance passed unanimously on September 3. Pre-hearing coverage (Hendersonville Times-News, July 23) described up to 12 months. End date is arithmetic. Packet: https://meetings.municode.com/adaHtmlDocument/index?cc=HVLNC&me=367f86a5a01442ae9c6e550a5792e6f2&ip=True . Henderson County itself has taken no action.
change_summary: Reported adopted 2026-09-03 for 12 months; the city's packet has the ordinance, the vote is not in minutes yet.
needs_confirmation: The city's own agenda and packet confirm the September 3 hearing and the draft ordinance, but the vote itself is reported only by a specialist newsletter. Minutes are not posted; the council's next regular meeting is October 1.

covers: new data centers
duration_label: 182 days, extended by one year on 2026-08-25
rationale: City had received developer inquiries and its unified development ordinance lacked definitions and standards for data centers; council wanted to study water-supply and energy-use impacts.
source_org: Queen City News / North State Journal
notes: UPDATE 2026-09-20: the extension is confirmed. Council voted on 2026-08-25 to extend the original 182-day moratorium (Ordinance 26-11, adopted 2026-02-24) by one full year; two outlets report the one-year term. The ordinance's printed end date has not been published, so 2027-08-25 is arithmetic from the extension vote. February minutes: https://www.cityofkm.com/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Minutes/_02242026-934
change_summary: Extension confirmed: one year from 2026-08-25.

covers: new or expanded data centers and cryptocurrency mining in zoned areas
duration_label: 60 days, extended by 90 days on 2026-09-03 (150 days total)
rationale: Commissioner Chad Hutchens: 'It's not anti-business. It's being reactive to where it's better for us, and it's better for whoever the developer may be down the road.'
notes: UPDATE 2026-09-24: commissioners extended the 60-day moratorium by 90 days at their September 3 meeting, after the Planning Board asked for more time; The Mount Airy News reported the extension in its coverage of the board's draft rules. Without it the record would have lapsed on the estimated September 14 date. The city has posted the September 3 agenda and packet but not the minutes, and both are scanned images, so no vote tally or printed end date is available; 2026-12-13 is arithmetic (150 days from July 16).
change_summary: Extended by 90 days on 2026-09-03, so it did not lapse in September.

covers: data center development
rationale: Residents raised water use, grid demand, noise, air pollution, health effects and the small number of permanent jobs; the county says no data center is approved or pending.
notes: NEW ACTION 2026-09-20: commissioners voted unanimously at a special meeting and public hearing on 2026-08-31. Commissioner David Walker proposed six months rather than the 12 the planning board recommended, with the board to revisit rules in February or March 2027. No printed end date published, so 2027-02-28 is arithmetic.
change_summary: Adopted a six-month moratorium 2026-08-31, two days after the snapshot.

covers: data centers, data processing facilities and cryptocurrency mining in unincorporated areas
duration_label: until 2027-06-30 or until new UDO rules are adopted
rationale: To study electricity and water demand, noise, environmental effects and land-use compatibility, and to draft unified development ordinance changes.
notes: NEW ACTION 2026-09-20: unanimous, effective immediately, running until 2027-06-30 or until the county adopts the UDO amendments, whichever comes first. Applies only to unincorporated Nash County; Rocky Mount and other municipalities keep their own authority. The towns of Bailey, Nashville, Spring Hope and Whitakers are separate records in this table.
change_summary: Adopted a moratorium 2026-09-08 for unincorporated areas, through 2027-06-30.

covers: data centers and cryptocurrency mining
rationale: Mayor Terry Mann and council cited water used for cooling, electricity demand and the effect on local resources; no data center has been proposed in the city.
notes: NEW RECORD 2026-09-20: the council voted 2026-08-25, effective immediately, running to 2027-08-25 or until the city adopts a zoning ordinance text amendment for these uses, whichever comes first. Columbus County itself has taken no action.
change_summary: Adopted a 12-month moratorium 2026-08-25, four days before the snapshot.

covers: permitting of data centers, data processing facilities, cryptocurrency mining and associated uses within the town and its extraterritorial jurisdiction
rationale: The town will use the pause to rewrite its unified development ordinance: where such facilities may be permitted, development standards, and rules addressing their impacts.
source_org: Town of Newport meeting notice / Public Radio East / WITN / WCTI / WNCT
notes: NEW RECORD 2026-09-24: the town's own notice for the September 10, 2026 Town Council meeting says it 'will include a Public Hearing to consider a request to enact a 1-year moratorium on the permitting of data centers'. Four outlets reported the approval on September 16 and 17, quoting Town Manager Michele Querry, and the council did not meet again until September 23, so the adoption date is September 10. No tally or printed end date was published; 2027-09-10 is arithmetic. Officials say it is not a permanent prohibition. Carteret County itself has taken no action.
change_summary: Adopted a one-year moratorium 2026-09-10; the town's meeting notice fixes the date.

covers: development approvals for critical digital infrastructure facilities, the town's term for data centers and crypto mining
rationale: Residents asked for a pause after DigiPower X bought land near a Duke Energy substation for a proposed AI data center; the town manager advised that a moratorium could run five months to a year while the ordinances are reviewed.
source_org: Town of Hildebran agenda and minutes / NC Data Centers newsletter
notes: NEW RECORD 2026-09-24: the July 27, 2026 minutes record that council 'was in agreement to begin the process for a twelve-month moratorium'. The August 24 agenda lists a public hearing and 'Consider Approval of Ordinance ... Instituting a Temporary Moratorium on Development Approvals for Critical Digital Infrastructure Facilities', with a presentation by the Poyner Spruill law firm. A specialist newsletter reports unanimous adoption. The September 28 agenda carries no moratorium item. Earlier in 2026 the town adopted permanent rules for these facilities. End date is arithmetic from August 24. Burke County itself has taken no action.
change_summary: Reported adopted 2026-08-24 for 12 months; the town's agenda confirms the hearing, the vote is not in minutes yet.
needs_confirmation: The town's own July 27 minutes and August 24 agenda confirm the council set out to adopt a twelve-month moratorium and held the hearing, but the vote is reported only by a specialist newsletter. August 24 minutes are not posted yet.

covers: new data center land uses
rationale: To give staff and council time to evaluate water, noise and infrastructure impacts after residents raised concerns about water use.
source_org: Citizen Portal meeting coverage / Rocky Mount Telegram
notes: NEW RECORD 2026-09-24: meeting coverage of the August 4, 2026 Town Council meeting records that council moved, seconded and carried an ordinance adopting a 12-month moratorium on new data center land uses, with development standards to guide later review, after public hearings in July and August. The Rocky Mount Telegram (September 9) confirms Nashville has a moratorium in place. No tally or printed end date published; 2027-08-04 is arithmetic. Nash County's own moratorium covers only unincorporated areas.
change_summary: Adopted a 12-month moratorium 2026-08-04, missed by the snapshot.

covers: data centers
rationale: Reported alongside Nashville and Bailey as one of three Nash County towns to pause data centers.
notes: NEW RECORD 2026-09-24: the Telegram's September 9 report on Nash County says 'the towns of Nashville, Bailey and Whitakers all have instituted moratoriums on data centers'. The town straddles the Nash and Edgecombe county line and is mapped by its municipal boundary. Edgecombe County's own two-year moratorium is a separate record.
change_summary: Reported to have a moratorium in place; date and length not published.
needs_confirmation: The Rocky Mount Telegram states the town has a moratorium and a specialist newsletter dates it to June 2026, but no date, length, ordinance or minutes could be found; the town's website lists no 2026 minutes.

covers: data center development
rationale: Council moved after a developer withdrew a southeast Raleigh data center proposal.
notes: UPDATE 2026-09-20: on 2026-09-15 the City Council directed the city attorney to draft a six-month moratorium, with a vote scheduled for 2026-10-06. Nothing is in force in Raleigh yet. Wake County itself has taken no action; Apex, Cary, Holly Springs and Wendell are separate records.
change_summary: Council directed a six-month moratorium to be drafted 2026-09-15; vote set for 2026-10-06.

covers: new data center projects in unincorporated Guilford County
rationale: Commissioners want time to write data center regulations; no application for a major facility is pending.
notes: UPDATE 2026-09-20: unanimous vote on 2026-09-17 to schedule a legislative public hearing for 2026-10-15 and to direct staff to prepare the ordinance. Nothing is in force at county level. Greensboro's own 180-day moratorium, adopted 2026-08-18, is a separate record.
change_summary: Voted 2026-09-17 to schedule an Oct. 15 hearing on a moratorium of up to 180 days.

covers: acceptance, processing and approval of all new data center applications (proposed)
rationale: Residents raised water use, energy demand and farmland loss.
notes: UPDATE 2026-09-20: the official hearing and vote set for September were postponed to give residents more time; an informal comment session went ahead. The final hearing and vote are scheduled for 2026-10-05 at 5:30 p.m. Nothing is in force.
change_summary: Vote on a proposed one-year moratorium postponed to 2026-10-05.

rationale: The board scheduled a legislative hearing on a pause days after approving an amended economic development agreement for an AI data center near Enfield.
notes: UPDATE 2026-09-20: The Daily Herald reports commissioners voted 5-1 to set a legislative hearing for 2026-10-19, with County Attorney Glynn Rollins noting the zoning ordinance does not regulate data centers; a specialist newsletter reports the same vote and date. The same board approved an amended economic development agreement covering a $1.7 million sale of about 251 acres at the 301 Industrial Site near Enfield to Quiet Data Centers Halifax, so the pause and the project are moving in parallel. The county's public notices page did not yet carry the hearing notice when checked on 2026-09-20. Nothing is in force.
change_summary: Voted 5-1 to schedule an Oct. 19 hearing on a possible moratorium.

covers: new hyperscale data center approvals (proposed)
rationale: Commissioners asked for a pause to study standards after rejecting a large data center in Rural Hall earlier in 2026.
source_org: Citizen Portal meeting coverage / Winston-Salem Journal
notes: UPDATE 2026-09-24: staff briefed the board on zoning, utility and legal limits (the county attorney warned that state law restricts downzoning) and were asked to return with tax estimates, legal language and milestones. A 4-3 straw vote directed staff to put a six-month moratorium on the September 28 agenda for discussion and possible action. Reports place the meeting on Monday, September 14, 2026; one meeting-coverage report says September 17 but was itself published September 15. The Winston-Salem Journal reported the board 'one step closer' to a six-month moratorium. Nothing is in force. Winston-Salem has taken no action.
change_summary: Straw vote 4-3 on 2026-09-14 to have staff prepare a possible six-month moratorium for 2026-09-28.

action_type: moratorium, public hearing held, outcome not published
covers: special use permits and other development approvals for data centers and cryptocurrency mining (proposed)
rationale: Public hearing 2026-09-08, 7:00 p.m., Perquimans County Library, covering a data center moratorium alongside a lawn maintenance ordinance and a flood prevention update.
source_org: Perquimans County official public hearing notice
notes: UPDATE 2026-09-24: the draft ordinance posted with the September 8 packet would impose a one-year moratorium from September 8, 2026 to September 7, 2027 on special use permits and other approvals for data centers and cryptocurrency mining, with a 12-month study schedule. It is drafted for adoption that night, but no minutes or coverage confirm a vote; the most recent posted minutes are from July. Treat this as an open question, not as a rejection.
change_summary: The 2026-09-08 hearing went ahead on a one-year draft, but the outcome has not been published.
needs_confirmation: The advertised public hearing on 2026-09-08 appears to have gone ahead, but the county has posted no minutes and no outlet covered it, so whether the moratorium was adopted is unknown.

covers: data centers (projects already in the development pipeline exempt)
rationale: Council wanted to 'review and understand and align on the facts' before setting growth policy; electricity costs and rates, water usage and noise raised around a proposed American Towers facility.
source_org: WFAE / City of Charlotte council agendas (Legistar)
notes: UPDATE 2026-09-20: the 150-day moratorium adopted 2026-06-08 still shows a printed end date of 2026-11-05. On 2026-09-08 the Transportation, Planning and Development Committee approved staff's request to seek nine more months to finish work on air-pollution monitoring and noise limits, and WFAE reported a full council vote set for 2026-09-14. The council's own agenda system (Legistar) records no data center or moratorium item among the 70 items on the 2026-09-14 business meeting agenda, whose other items carry recorded actions, nor on the 2026-09-21 zoning and special meetings, so the extension had not been voted as of 2026-09-20.
change_summary: A nine-month extension is still pending: it never reached the council's 2026-09-14 agenda.
expiration_note: A nine-month extension has been proposed but not voted: no data center item appears on the council's published agendas through 2026-09-21. If it passes before 2026-11-05, this end date moves.

covers: data centers
rationale: Council postponed a decision on the planning department's recommended one-year moratorium to a September 2026 meeting; Mayor Ed Hatley suggested possibly shortening any moratorium to 3-6 months and hiring a consultant.
notes: UPDATE 2026-09-20: the council voted 3-1 on 2026-08-06 to postpone the planning department's recommended one-year moratorium and to resume the public hearing in September 2026. No coverage of a September vote was found, so the decision appears to be still open. Lincoln County itself has taken no action.
change_summary: Re-checked: no report of the September vote the council promised.

covers: data centers
rationale: 'A 12-month moratorium will ensure that we could have adequate time to develop regulations for these types of developments'; existing zoning allowed approval without full review.
notes: UPDATE 2026-09-20: the 12-month moratorium adopted 2026-05-18 stands. At the commissioners' 2026-09-14 meeting a final draft unified development ordinance was presented that would prohibit data centers outright; it has not been adopted. Reported by The Daily Advance ('EC eyes data center ordinance as county moves to ban them').
change_summary: Still in effect; a draft UDO that would ban data centers outright went public 2026-09-14.

covers: data centers, crypto mining facilities and similar uses
rationale: Commissioners cited grid capacity, water use of roughly 1.5 million gallons per day, diesel generator noise and air pollution, and minimal job creation.
source_org: Watauga County Board of Commissioners minutes / Watauga Democrat / WataugaOnline
notes: UPDATE 2026-09-24: the county's April 21, 2026 minutes are now retrievable. After the public hearing, Commissioner Marsh moved and Vice-Chairman Castle seconded a moratorium on data centers; the vote was 5-0, then amended 5-0 to add the statutory findings: it applies to data centers, crypto mining facilities and similar uses, terminates one year after adoption, and directs planning staff to draft rules under the High Impact Land Use ordinance. The minutes give the term, not a calendar date, so 2027-04-21 is arithmetic. The Town of Boone's own moratorium (March 23) is a separate record.
change_summary: County minutes now retrieved: adopted 5-0 on 2026-04-21 for one year.

covers: commercial data centers with a peak power demand of 2 megawatts or more, in unincorporated Clay County
rationale: The ordinance states its purpose as protecting the health, safety and general welfare of county residents by prohibiting commercial data centers, including those supporting artificial intelligence.
source_org: Citizen Portal meeting coverage / Clay County Progress / Clay County ordinances page
notes: UPDATE 2026-09-24: coverage of the January 8, 2026 board meeting records County Attorney Merinda Woody reading the ordinance after a public hearing, a motion by Commissioner Clay Logan seconded by Commissioner Randy Nichols, and a 5-0 vote. The Clay County Progress published the ordinance text: commercial data centers of 2 megawatts or more are prohibited from establishing, constructing, expanding or operating in unincorporated Clay County, effective January 8, 2026 (that page was indexed by search engines but returned an error when checked). The county's ordinances page lists the ordinance as an image-only PDF. Do not confuse with Clay County, Florida, which adopted a separate one-year moratorium in 2026.
change_summary: Adoption date and permanence now documented: 5-0 on 2026-01-08, a permanent ban on 2 MW and larger.

covers: data centers (a definition critics called broad enough to reach ordinary business computer networks)
rationale: Modeled on Spring Hope's one-year moratorium; meant to block AI data centers because of their electricity and water use.
notes: UPDATE 2026-09-24: no longer a single-tracker claim. The Spring Hope Enterprise (May 26, 2026, Corey Friedman) reports the Board of Commissioners passed Resolution 2026-02 on Monday, May 18, 2026 by a 3-1 vote, presented by zoning administrator Shawn Lucas; Commissioner David Evans objected that the definition of data center was too broad. End date is arithmetic (10 months). Nash County's own moratorium covers only unincorporated areas, so this record stands on its own.
change_summary: Confirmed by the Spring Hope Enterprise: 3-1 vote on 2026-05-18 for 10 months.
